name: Acute Coronary Syndrome
keyManagement: dual antiplatelet + anticoagulation + PCI/thrombolysis

name: Stable Angina
keyManagement: GTN PRN + beta-blocker or CCB + statin + antiplatelet

name: Heart Failure
keyManagement: ACEi/ARB + beta-blocker + diuretic + MRA + SGLT2i

name: Atrial Fibrillation
keyManagement: rate/rhythm control + anticoagulation if CHA2DS2-VASc >=2

name: Aortic Dissection
keyManagement: urgent surgical referral (type A) / BP control (type B)

name: Pulmonary Embolism
keyManagement: anticoagulation + thrombolysis if massive

name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
keyManagement: antibiotics per CURB-65 severity + supportive

name: Acute Exacerbation of COPD
keyManagement: bronchodilators + systemic steroids + antibiotics if purulent sputum + NIV

name: Asthma Exacerbation
keyManagement: salbutamol nebulisers + ipratropium + systemic steroids + IV magnesium

name: Tension Pneumothorax
investigations: clinical diagnosis — do not delay for imaging
keyManagement: immediate needle decompression then chest drain

name: Acute Stroke — Ischaemic
keyManagement: thrombolysis if within 4.5h + thrombectomy if LVO within 24h

name: Subarachnoid Haemorrhage
keyManagement: urgent neurosurgical referral for coiling/clipping + nimodipine

name: Bacterial Meningitis
investigations: CT head if raised ICP signs
keyManagement: immediate IV ceftriaxone + dexamethasone; do not delay for LP

name: Migraine
keyManagement: acute: triptan + NSAID; prophylaxis: propranolol/amitriptyline/topiramate

name: Epileptic Seizure
keyManagement: benzodiazepines (acute); maintenance: levetiracetam/sodium valproate/lamotrigine

name: Upper GI Bleed
keyManagement: resuscitation + PPI infusion + urgent endoscopy + terlipressin if variceal

name: Acute Pancreatitis
keyManagement: aggressive fluid resuscitation + analgesia + NBM initially + treat cause

name: Acute Appendicitis
keyManagement: appendicectomy (laparoscopic preferred) + antibiotics if complicated

name: Acute Cholecystitis
keyManagement: antibiotics + cholecystectomy within 72h if fit

name: Bowel Obstruction
keyManagement: NBM + NG decompression + IV fluids + surgery if strangulation

name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
typicalFeatures: worse with food (gastric) or relieved by food (duodenal)
keyManagement: PPI + H. pylori eradication if positive + stop NSAIDs

name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Flare
keyManagement: 5-ASA (mild UC) / IV steroids (severe) / biologics if refractory

name: Acute Kidney Injury
keyManagement: treat cause + fluid resuscitation + stop nephrotoxins + RRT if refractory

name: Lower UTI
keyManagement: empirical antibiotics (nitrofurantoin/trimethoprim) + hydration

name: Pyelonephritis
keyManagement: IV antibiotics + fluids + drainage if obstructed

name: Renal Colic / Nephrolithiasis
keyManagement: analgesia (diclofenac/paracetamol) + tamsulosin if <=10mm + urological intervention

name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
keyManagement: IV fluids + fixed-rate insulin infusion + potassium replacement + monitor

name: Hypoglycaemia
keyManagement: oral glucose if conscious / IV dextrose or IM glucagon if unconscious

name: Thyrotoxicosis / Thyroid Storm
keyManagement: beta-blocker + carbimazole; storm: IV hydrocortisone + propranolol + Lugol iodine

name: Addisonian Crisis
keyManagement: immediate IV hydrocortisone 100mg + IV saline + dextrose if hypoglycaemic

name: Sepsis
keyManagement: Sepsis Six within 1h: cultures + IV antibiotics + IV fluids + lactate + urine output + oxygen

name: Cellulitis
keyManagement: flucloxacillin + elevation + surgical review if necrotising

name: Deep Vein Thrombosis
keyManagement: anticoagulation (DOAC preferred) for >=3 months

name: Anaphylaxis
investigations: clinical diagnosis — do not delay treatment
keyManagement: IM adrenaline 0.5mg + high-flow oxygen + IV fluid bolus + chlorphenamine + hydrocortisone

name: Acute Limb Ischaemia
typicalFeatures: 6 Ps: pain, pallor, pulselessness, paraesthesia, paralysis, perishing cold
keyManagement: heparin + urgent vascular surgery (embolectomy/bypass/thrombolysis)

name: Cauda Equina Syndrome
keyManagement: emergency surgical decompression within 48h + high-dose dexamethasone

name: Spinal Cord Compression
keyManagement: dexamethasone 16mg + urgent neurosurgical/oncology review + radiotherapy/surgery

name: Guillain-Barre Syndrome
keyManagement: IVIg or plasma exchange + ICU if FVC declining + physiotherapy

name: Status Epilepticus
keyManagement: IV lorazepam then phenytoin/levetiracetam then anaesthetic agents if refractory

name: Acute Liver Failure
keyManagement: NAC if paracetamol + ITU + King College criteria for transplant listing

name: Ectopic Pregnancy
keyManagement: surgical (laparoscopic salpingectomy) if ruptured; methotrexate if unruptured

name: Pre-eclampsia
keyManagement: labetalol/nifedipine + MgSO4 if severe + plan delivery

name: Testicular Torsion
investigations: clinical diagnosis — do not delay for imaging
keyManagement: emergency surgical exploration and fixation within 6h

name: Acute Gout
keyManagement: NSAID or colchicine (acute) + allopurinol prophylaxis

name: Septic Arthritis
keyManagement: IV antibiotics + joint washout/aspiration

name: Hip Fracture
keyManagement: surgical fixation within 36h + VTE prophylaxis + bone protection

name: Lumbar Disc Herniation
keyManagement: conservative (analgesia + physiotherapy) then epidural/microdiscectomy if refractory

name: Acute Compartment Syndrome
keyManagement: emergency fasciotomy; remove all casts/dressings

name: Rheumatoid Arthritis Flare
keyManagement: DMARDs (methotrexate first-line) + short-course steroids + biologics if refractory

name: Giant Cell Arteritis
keyManagement: high-dose prednisolone immediately (60mg if visual symptoms) — do not wait for biopsy

name: Spontaneous Pneumothorax
keyManagement: conservative if small; aspiration or chest drain if large/secondary/symptomatic

name: Pleural Effusion
keyManagement: treat underlying cause + therapeutic aspiration/drain if symptomatic

name: GORD / Oesophagitis
keyManagement: lifestyle modification + PPI + fundoplication if refractory

name: Acute Diverticulitis
keyManagement: antibiotics + clear fluids + surgery if complicated

name: Mesenteric Ischaemia
typicalFeatures: severe abdominal pain out of proportion to examination
keyManagement: fluid resuscitation + anticoagulation + urgent surgical/IR revascularisation

name: Acute Viral Hepatitis
keyManagement: supportive + notify public health + monitor for acute liver failure

name: Malaria
investigations: thick and thin blood films x3
keyManagement: IV artesunate if severe / oral artemether-lumefantrine if uncomplicated

name: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
keyManagement: RIPE for 2 months then RI for 4 months + pyridoxine

name: Infective Endocarditis
keyManagement: prolonged IV antibiotics (4-6 weeks) + surgical valve replacement if complicated

name: Pericarditis
keyManagement: NSAID + colchicine + steroids if recurrent; pericardiocentesis if tamponade

name: NSTEMI
keyManagement: dual antiplatelet + fondaparinux + statin + beta-blocker + angiography within 72h

name: Hypertensive Emergency
keyManagement: IV labetalol or GTN infusion; reduce BP by no more than 25% in first hour

name: Cardiac Tamponade
typicalFeatures: Beck triad: hypotension + muffled heart sounds + raised JVP
keyManagement: urgent pericardiocentesis + IV fluids + treat underlying cause

name: ARDS
keyManagement: lung-protective ventilation (6ml/kg IBW) + prone positioning + conservative fluid + treat cause

name: Acute Urinary Retention
keyManagement: urethral catheter + monitor for post-obstructive diuresis + alpha-blocker

name: Acute Psychosis
investigations: exclude organic: FBC, U&E, TFTs, glucose, calcium, urine drug screen, CT head
keyManagement: de-escalation + oral antipsychotic (olanzapine/haloperidol) + psychiatric assessment

name: Delirium
investigations: confusion screen: FBC, U&E, CRP, LFTs, TFTs, calcium, glucose, urinalysis, CXR
keyManagement: treat underlying cause + reorientation + avoid antipsychotics unless distressed

name: Paracetamol Overdose
keyManagement: IV N-acetylcysteine per nomogram + psychiatric assessment + King College criteria

name: Opioid Overdose
keyManagement: IV/IM naloxone (titrate to respiratory rate) + maintain airway + prolonged observation

name: Alcohol Withdrawal / Delirium Tremens
keyManagement: chlordiazepoxide reducing regimen + Pabrinex + electrolyte correction

name: Hyperkalaemia
redFlagFeatures: ECG changes (peaked T waves, broad QRS)
keyManagement: IV calcium gluconate + insulin-dextrose + salbutamol neb + treat cause + consider dialysis

name: Hyponatraemia
keyManagement: fluid restrict (SIADH) / IV saline (hypovolaemic); hypertonic saline if severe

name: Rhabdomyolysis
keyManagement: aggressive IV fluid resuscitation + treat hyperkalaemia + monitor for AKI

name: Sickle Cell Vaso-occlusive Crisis
keyManagement: IV fluids + strong analgesia (opioids) + oxygen + antibiotics if febrile + exchange transfusion if ACS

name: DIC
keyManagement: treat underlying cause + cryoprecipitate + platelets + FFP

name: Neutropenic Sepsis
keyManagement: immediate IV piperacillin-tazobactam within 1h + antifungal if not responding

name: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
keyManagement: stop causative drug + transfer to burns unit + wound care + IVIg/cyclosporin

name: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
keyManagement: pilocarpine + timolol + IV acetazolamide + urgent laser iridotomy

name: Retinal Detachment
keyManagement: urgent ophthalmology for surgical repair (vitrectomy/scleral buckle)

name: Peritonsillar Abscess (Quinsy)
investigations: CT neck if deep space infection suspected
keyManagement: needle aspiration or I&D + IV antibiotics + analgesia

name: Epiglottitis
keyManagement: secure airway + IV ceftriaxone + dexamethasone + humidified oxygen

name: Diabetic Foot Infection
keyManagement: broad-spectrum antibiotics + surgical debridement + offloading + vascular assessment

name: Wernicke Encephalopathy
keyManagement: IV Pabrinex (high-dose thiamine) for 5 days minimum + thiamine before glucose

name: Necrotising Fasciitis
keyManagement: emergency surgical debridement + IV broad-spectrum antibiotics + ITU

name: Placental Abruption
keyManagement: emergency delivery + IV fluids/blood products + correct coagulopathy

name: Postpartum Haemorrhage
keyManagement: 4 Ts: Tone (oxytocin + ergometrine) + Tissue + Trauma + Thrombin

name: Peripheral Arterial Disease
keyManagement: risk-factor modification + supervised exercise + antiplatelet + revascularisation if critical

name: Cholangitis — Ascending
typicalFeatures: Charcot triad: fever + jaundice + RUQ pain
keyManagement: IV antibiotics + IV fluids + urgent biliary drainage (ERCP) within 24h

name: Perforated Viscus
keyManagement: IV resuscitation + IV antibiotics + urgent surgical repair

name: Myasthenia Gravis Crisis
keyManagement: intubation if FVC declining + IVIg or plasma exchange + pyridostigmine

name: Hepatic Encephalopathy
keyManagement: lactulose + rifaximin + treat precipitant + avoid sedatives

name: Variceal Bleeding
keyManagement: terlipressin + IV antibiotics + band ligation at OGD + TIPS if refractory

name: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
keyManagement: 100% oxygen via non-rebreather + hyperbaric oxygen if severe

name: Spinal Epidural Abscess
investigations: urgent MRI whole spine with contrast
keyManagement: urgent surgical drainage + prolonged IV antibiotics (6-8 weeks)

name: BPPV
typicalFeatures: brief episodes of vertigo with head movement
keyManagement: Epley manoeuvre + Brandt-Daroff exercises

name: Herpes Zoster (Shingles)
investigations: PCR of vesicle fluid if uncertain
keyManagement: aciclovir/valaciclovir within 72h + analgesia + ophthalmology if V1

name: Pneumocystis Pneumonia
keyManagement: co-trimoxazole high-dose 21 days + prednisolone if PaO2 below 9.3kPa

name: Burns — Major
keyManagement: Parkland formula fluids + analgesia + wound care + early intubation if airway + escharotomy if circumferential

name: Multiple Sclerosis Relapse
typicalFeatures: new or worsening neurological symptoms lasting over 24h
investigations: MRI brain and spine with gadolinium
keyManagement: IV methylprednisolone 1g/day for 3-5 days + disease-modifying therapy

name: Heat Stroke
keyManagement: rapid cooling (evaporative + ice packs) + IV fluids + benzodiazepines for shivering

name: Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis
keyManagement: IV ceftriaxone + IV albumin + secondary prophylaxis

name: Aortic Stenosis — Decompensated
keyManagement: avoid vasodilators in acute; TAVI or surgical AVR when symptomatic

name: Massive Haemoptysis
typicalFeatures: coughing large volumes of blood over 200ml/24h
keyManagement: lie affected side down + oxygen + tranexamic acid + IR (BAE) or surgery

name: Urticaria — Acute
keyManagement: antihistamine (cetirizine/fexofenadine) + avoid trigger + adrenaline if anaphylaxis

name: Psoriasis Flare
keyManagement: emollients + topical steroids/vitamin D + phototherapy + DMARDs/biologics if severe

name: Acute Otitis Externa
keyManagement: topical antibiotic/steroid drops + ear toilet + oral antibiotics if spreading

name: Acute Otitis Media
keyManagement: analgesia + watchful waiting 48-72h; amoxicillin if severe/bilateral/under 2

name: Ischaemic Colitis
keyManagement: supportive + surgery if gangrenous/peritonitis

name: Phaeochromocytoma Crisis
keyManagement: alpha-blockade first (phenoxybenzamine) then beta-blockade + surgical resection

name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
keyManagement: stop causative drug + supportive wound care + ophthalmology + consider IVIg

name: Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy
keyManagement: supportive + beta-blocker + ACEi + anticoagulation if LV thrombus

name: HIV Seroconversion
keyManagement: early ART initiation + partner notification + STI screen

name: Meniere Disease
keyManagement: low-salt diet + betahistine + prochlorperazine PRN

name: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
keyManagement: weight loss + acetazolamide + optic nerve sheath fenestration or VP shunt if vision threatened

name: Hypothermia
keyManagement: gradual rewarming + warm IV fluids + monitoring + CPR if arrest (continue until warm)

name: Myxoedema Coma
keyManagement: IV levothyroxine + IV hydrocortisone + rewarming + ITU care

name: Pancreatitis — Chronic
typicalFeatures: chronic epigastric pain radiating to back
keyManagement: pain management + PERT (Creon) + fat-soluble vitamins + diabetes management + alcohol cessation
